In-depth program, no shortage of reps, unreal learning curve.

parentQA.a: Jack, then Ryan. Both have Jeremiah's number. No account manager, no call center. We stay mid-size so he's never in a bigger client's shadow.
The NFLPA caps agent fees at 3% of the playing contract, and ours go in writing before anything is signed. Nothing is paid up front, and fees are only owed on money he actually receives.

parentQA.q: How do you protect what he earns?
parentQA.a: Ryan writes the guarantee and injury language. We screen every advisor before he meets them, coordinate taxes, set up disability insurance and build a year-one budget. A good first contract is only the start.

parentQA.q: What happens if he gets hurt?
parentQA.a: Injury settlements, grievances and second opinions are ours to handle. Disability coverage is in place before the first snap.

parentQA.q: What if he's not drafted where we hope?
parentQA.a: It happens, and it isn't the end. Kristian Welch signed with us as an undrafted free agent in 2020 and has played six NFL seasons. The slot decides the first contract; preparation decides the second.

In business since 1986, with six clients who became the highest paid at their position. Jack Tabb played the position, and Ryan Hays is a licensed attorney. We're happy to connect you with current client families.

handle: Rookie deal, extensions, guarantees, fine appeals, grievances. Ryan writes the language.

ask.h: Let's sit down and walk it through
ask.lede: This page is the outline. In person we'll walk you from senior season to draft night and into your second contract: the Nashville plan, what your slot could be worth, who handles what. Bring your family and your questions.

comp.lede: A tight end who blocks like the linebacker he used to be and breaks tackles after the catch. Kraft built his career on exactly that, and he did it with us.
comp.foot: Kraft went from a Round 3 pick to one of the top-paid tight ends in the league. That's the road we'd map for you.
